Be Part of the PCBWay 7th Project Design Contest! by: PCBWay Sep 03,2024 <dynamic-value> <dynamic-value> Posted in News We are glad to announce that PCBWay 7th Project Design Contest has arrived. Prior to this, PCBWay successfully held six design contests. In each contest, we saw many eye-catching projects shared by outstanding and creative electronic engineers and enthusiasts. PCBWay 7th Project Design Contest will continue the previous purpose, which is to encourage more and more people to explore the charm of electronic design and participate in it. PCBWay 7th Project Design Contest: https://www.pcbway.com/activity/7th-project-design-contest.html . In this contest, in addition to the two themes of Electronic Project and Mechanical Project that have appeared before, we also introduced STM32 Project, hoping to give designers more room to perform. The contest will start on September 2nd, 2024, and project submissions will be accepted until January 19th, 2025. After this, the judging phase will begin, and the final winners will be announced on the PCBWay Blog on March 10th, 2025. Two ways to participate in the contest: Go to the contest page, find the Participate Now button and click it. In this case, the submitted project will automatically be entered into the competition; participants only need to select the theme of entry. Please note that if you are submitting a mechanical project, please switch to the CNC |3D Printing Project page. After filling in all the project information, simply click "Submit" at the bottom of the page. Go to the SharedProject Community ( https://www.pcbway.com/project/shareproject/ ) and click Create a project. Select the theme you are going to participate in. Similarly, if you are submitting a mechanical project, please switch to the CNC |3D Printing Project page. Hint: Sharing complete project files, including Gerber, BOM, Centroid file, schematics, 3D files, and so on will increase the chances of receiving a higher score. Awards and corresponding prizes: The First Prize : 1 winner, $1500 Cash + $200 Coupon + A Palm-sized Robot Dog*1 The Second Prize : 2 winners, $1000 Cash + $100 Coupon + Raspberry Pi 5 4GB *1 The Third Prize : 3 winners, $500 Cash + $50 Coupon + OpenMV4 H7 R2 Cam Smart Camera *1 Popular Design Prize : 10 winners, $100 Cash + $20 Coupon + $10 3D Printing Coupon + Multimeter ZTY890DPro *1 Participation Prize : Raspberry Pi Pico * 1 STM32 Great Project Prize : Six-Claw Multifunctional Aluminum Alloy Soldering Table *1 For more detailed information about the contest, please refer to: https://www.pcbway.com/activity/7th-project-design-contest.html . If there are any questions or suggestions, feel free to leave a comment below.We wish you the best of luck and look forward to your innovative designs! Verify Now Blog > Corporate Social Responsibility of PCBWay Corporate Social Responsibility of PCBWay by: PCBWay May 30,2025 <dynamic-value> <dynamic-value> Posted in News PCBWay recognizes the significant role it plays within the supply chain and broader society, along with the potential impact of its operations. To this end, we have established and strictly enforce the following principles, which not only govern our own conduct but also set clear expectations for our partners. Our goal is to ensure full legal and regulatory compliance, promote long-term sustainability, and generate a positive impact on society. Human Rights and Labor Protection No employment of individuals below the legal working age; all forms of forced or bonded labor are strictly prohibited. Discrimination and harassment in the workplace are not tolerated; an inclusive work environment for persons with disabilities is encouraged. Employees must be provided with fair compensation and reasonable rest periods, and their rights to freedom of association and collective bargaining must be respected. Business Ethics and Compliance Offering, promising, soliciting, or accepting any form of bribery is strictly prohibited; effective conflict of interest management and whistleblowing mechanisms must be in place. All financial and business records must accurately, completely, and truthfully reflect the underlying transactions. Full compliance with international sanctions, export controls, and other applicable laws and regulations is required. Supply Chain Responsibility and Sustainable Procurement PCBWay and its partners are required to extend the principles outlined in this document to all levels of entities within the supply chain. Priority should be given to selecting partners that are legally compliant, socially responsible, and committed to sustainable development. Identify social, labor, and environmental risks related to operations, and develop corresponding control and mitigation measures. Encourage partners to prioritize local sourcing to support regional economic development and job creation. Environmental Protection and Workplace Safety Actively implement environmental protection measures and continuously promote energy conservation and emission reduction; Ensure that all waste and hazardous materials are disposed of in accordance with relevant laws and regulations. The procurement or use of prohibited materials is not allowed. Provide employees with a safe working environment and health support mechanisms to prevent occupational injuries and health risks. PCBWay has fully adopted the DHL GoGreen transportation service in 2025 to reduce carbon emissions in the supply chain and promote the development of a green supply chain, with an initial target of reducing emissions by 30%. Information Protection and Transparent Governance Establish a comprehensive security system to strictly protect the confidentiality of customer data, drawings, and other business information. Comply with relevant laws and regulations to safeguard the personal data of customers and employees. Ensure that financial records are true, accurate, and complete, and prohibit any illegal activities. PCBWay will ensure the implementation of the above principles in actual cooperation and reserves the right to take action against any violations. When an individual or company purchases goods from an overseas supplier, U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) considers them the ultimate importer. The ultimate importer can clear the goods or have a Customs Broker clear them on their behalf. If the supplier hires a carrier that provides door to door service, the carrier service usually has brokers in their supply chain to clear the goods on behalf of the ultimate importer. If a formal entry is required, CBP regulations require the broker to put the ultimate importer's identification number on the CBP Form 7501- Entry Summary. The ultimate importer's identification number is either the Employers Identification Number (EIN) tax identification number assigned by the Internal Revenue Service (IRS) or the importer's social security number. The EIN is issued for the purpose of tax administration and are not intended for participation in any other activities (e.g., tax lien auction or sales, lotteries). For additional information about EIN, please visit the IRS web page "Apply for an Employer Identification (EIN) Online." Goods are usually cleared informally when they are for personal use, under $2500 in value, and are not in commercial quantities. A formal entry is usually required for commercial importations valued over $2,500. Because many foreign merchants are aware that CBP requires an identification number for the ultimate importer for formal entries, they will often request the purchaser's social security number to include on export documents that the broker will subsequently rely on to prepare the CBP entry. It should be noted that paperwork for goods sent by courier service does ask for an importer number, whether the import qualifies for an informal entry or not. Courier services file CBP entries electronically, and the software system they use requires an identification number to be provided for the recipient of the goods. If an identification number is not provided, the courier service is required to file a paper entry, which is extremely time-consuming and in the world of "Overnight Delivery" not practical. The end result is that most courier services will not accept packages for international delivery to U.S. residents if a recipient's identification number is not provided by the shipper. Goods sent through the international postal service that are under $2500 in value generally do not require an importer number to be cleared through CBP. Note: Regarding why your social security number/tax ID number/IRS number/importer number is needed when shipping, please check out this official article for explanation: Why is an overseas supplier asking for my social security number/tax ID number/IRS number/importer number? ============================================================================================== by the way： Importers - Why is an overseas supplier asking for my social security number/tax ID number/IRS number/importer number? When an individual or company purchases goods from an overseas supplier, U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) considers them the ultimate importer. The ultimate importer can clear the goods or have a Customs Broker clear them on their behalf. If the supplier hires a carrier that provides door to door service, the carrier service usually has brokers in their supply chain to clear the goods on behalf of the ultimate importer. If a formal entry is required, CBP regulations require the broker to put the ultimate importer's identification number on the CBP Form 7501- Entry Summary. The ultimate importer's identification number is either the Employers Identification Number (EIN) tax identification number assigned by the Internal Revenue Service (IRS) or the importer's social security number. The EIN is issued for the purpose of tax administration and are not intended for participation in any other activities (e.g., tax lien auction or sales, lotteries). For additional information about EIN, please visit the IRS web page "Apply for an Employer Identification (EIN) Online." Goods are usually cleared informally when they are for personal use, under $2500 in value, and are not in commercial quantities. A formal entry is usually required for commercial importations valued over $2,500. Because many foreign merchants are aware that CBP requires an identification number for the ultimate importer for formal entries, they will often request the purchaser's social security number to include on export documents that the broker will subsequently rely on to prepare the CBP entry. It should be noted that paperwork for goods sent by courier service does ask for an importer number, whether the import qualifies for an informal entry or not. Courier services file CBP entries electronically, and the software system they use requires an identification number to be provided for the recipient of the goods. If an identification number is not provided, the courier service is required to file a paper entry, which is extremely time-consuming and in the world of "Overnight Delivery" not practical. The end result is that most courier services will not accept packages for international delivery to U.S. residents if a recipient's identification number is not provided by the shipper. Goods sent through the international postal service that are under $2500 in value generally do not require an importer number to be cleared through CBP. It’s Trickier Than You Think. But because of an ever-changing patchwork of trade rules, not every product will be charged an astronomical tariff, trade lawyers, customs brokers and importers say. In some cases, tariffs will pile on other tariffs. In other instances, they can reduce costs, while other times they can cancel out new ones. The event will take place from September 9 to 11, 2026, at Songdo Convensia in Incheon, South Korea. During the exhibition, PCBWay will be at Booth R310, where visitors can meet our team, learn more about our PCB and electronics manufacturing capabilities, and discuss solutions for their upcoming projects. About KPCA Show 2026 KPCA Show 2026, officially known as the International Semiconductor Circuits and Advanced Packaging Show, will be held at Songdo Convensia in Incheon from September 9 to 11, 2026. The exhibition is organized by the Korea Semiconductor Packaging and Circuits Association (KPCA) and Incheon Metropolitan City. The show brings together companies and professionals from across the electronics manufacturing industry, with exhibition areas covering advanced semiconductor substrates, semiconductor packaging, plating and surface treatment, reliability equipment, automotive electronics, and motion control and collaborative robotics. As PCB technology continues to evolve toward higher density, greater reliability, and increasingly complex applications, KPCA Show provides an opportunity for industry professionals to explore new technologies and connect with manufacturing partners. Meet PCBWay at Booth R310 At Booth R310, the PCBWay team will be available to introduce our manufacturing capabilities and discuss how we can support projects from prototype development to production. Meet PCBWay at electronica 2024! by: PCBWay Oct 18,2024 <dynamic-value> <dynamic-value> Posted in News Once again, we welcome the famous technology event electronica in Munich, Germany! Since the first exhibition was held in 1964, electronica has gradually grown and now covers the entire world of electronics, including the micro- and nano-worlds of semiconductor and micro systems technology, as well as measurement and sensor technology, display technology and vehicle electronics, etc., which is the best choice for any technology enthusiasts and industry practitioners. PCBWay has participated in theelectronica many times and has received a warm response every time. At the exhibition, everyone has the opportunity to get close to our various products and fully evaluate the performance and quality of our products, which is far beyond the scope of online communication. On-site interaction gives us the opportunity to answer everyone's questions in a timely manner and help them understand the products more comprehensively, thereby accelerating the process of cooperation. Therefore, after the exhibition, we not only strengthened our cooperation with existing customers, but also successfully attracted the attention of many new potential partners. PCBWay will certainly not be absent from this year's exhibition.In addition, in order to give everyone a better exhibition experience and also to show how much importance PCBWay attaches to this exhibition, this year we made some innovations: Time: 2024.11.12-2024.11.15 Location: Trade Fair Center Messe München, Germany PCBWay Booth No.: A1.163 Highlights: Color- printed Boards In addition to the PCB series products, 3D printed parts and sheet metal parts that we have been displaying in the past, we will also bring the latest color-printed board samples. This new product has attracted the attention and interest of many customers, so we hope to take this opportunity to let everyone experience the excellent effect and quality of the color-printed board in person. New Booth We focused on designing the on-site booth as well. We expanded the booth area to 5m x 14m, providing a larger activity space, and also improved the sophistication of various details, in order to make the overall atmosphere more professional and make everyone's visiting experience more comfortable. Verify Now Blog > PCBWay Fabrication Toolkit for Kicad PCBWay Fabrication Toolkit for Kicad by: PCBWay Oct 11,2023 <dynamic-value> <dynamic-value> Posted in News Recently, PCBWay added a plug-in called PCBWay Fabrication Toolkit to Kicad: With just one click of the mouse, four files can be exported from the layout file automatically: Gerber file, IPC-Netlist file, BOM file and Pick and Place file, which can significantly improves the efficiency of pre-production work. Installation from the Official KiCad Repositories After installation, the plugin will appear on the right side of the navigation bar. And users can use it to export all the production files with just a click. Process demonstration： Sending the files to PCBWay, and they can be used for production after being reviewed by the staff. Note: If you want to place an assembly order, please be sure to add MPN information to the BOM. This can help the quoter source the devices you need more accurately. Manual installation Except for the way mentioned before, you can also download the latest ZIP file from https://github.com/pcbway/PCBWay-Fabrication-Toolkit-for-KiCad: Open the "Plugin and Content Manager" from the main window of KiCad and install the ZIP file via "Install from File". About BOM Through BOM files, we can get all information of the components used in your design. In order to speed up the quotation process, we need this information: 1. Designator (necessary) 2. Quantity (necessary) 3. MPN/Part Number (necessary) 4. Package/Footprint (necessary) 5. Manufacturer (optional) 6. Description/value (optional) If you have more suggestions, please leave a message below, PCBWay has committed to providing everyone with high-quality services. Verify Now Blog > PCBWay Plug-In for KiCad PCBWay Plug-In for KiCad by: Anson Apr 01,2022 Posted in News Kicad PCB design Send your layout to PCBWay for instant production with just one click. Have you ever thought that when you complete the design on KiCad, you can place an order on pcbway with just one click? Now this idea is finally achieved (it's not an April Fool's joke). When you click PCBWay Plug-in button on Kicad, we will export these files in your project ( Please make sure you have installed the latest version of the plugin released at 2026 )： 1.Gerber files in correct format for production 2.IPC-Netlist file 3.Bom-file that includes all information of components 4.Pick and Place-file used in assembly You can click "Save to Cart" to place an order immediately after uploading the files( usually only takes a few seconds), our engineers will double check the files before the production. Note:We have updated plugin for Kicad 10,you could also place assembly order directly now. But we need to get the component "Manufacture Part Number". Please confirm you run the "Update Board from Schematic" and install the latest version of the plugin. ﻿ Installation from the official KiCad repositories Just open the "Plugin and Content Manager" from the KiCad main menu an install the "PCBWay Plug-in for KiCad" plugin from the selection list. Manual installation You can also download the latest ZIP file from https://github.com/pcbway/PCBWay-Plug-in-for-Kicad , then open the "Plugin and Content Manager" from the main window of KiCad and install the ZIP file via "Install from File". About Bom We can get all information of components used in your design ( please make sure you have installed the latest version of the plugin) . In order to speed up the quotation of components, we need this information: 1. Designator (necessary) 2. Quantity (necessary) 3. MPN/Part Number (necessary) 4. Package/Footprint (necessary) 5. Manufacturer (optional) 6. Description/value (optional) You just need to add the properties in your schematic like the picture shows: As a sponsor of KiCad, we will always support its development. Note: Thanks to the open source community. Since we are not skilled enough to edit on github at the moment, any feedback or questions please contact with anson@pcbway.com Enter the year of your birth and check your Chinese Zodiac. Join us Wanna be a dedicated PCBWay writer? We definately look forward to having you with us. Unlock Color PCB Printing with PCBWay! by: PCBWay Mar 08,2024 <dynamic-value> <dynamic-value> Posted in News Color PCB Printing PCBWay Service Nowadays, traditional PCB printing technology can no longer meet the aesthetic requirements of modern circuit board production. To better fulfill customers' design needs, we are pleased to announce that PCBWay has introduced UV printing equipment. This equipment utilizes UV-curable inks to achieve high-quality image printing on various materials, including fiberglass boards, metal substrates, ceramic substrates, flexible boards, and rigid-flex boards. Entrance https://www.pcbway.com/orderonline.aspx Prerequisites for Ordering Maximum size for a single piece: 270*470MM; Selection of background soldermask color required. Design Specifications Drill holes, traces, soldermasks, and outline designs must comply with specifications. Avoid placing colored characters in areas with solder mask openings, such as surface-mount pads or through-hole pads. What kind of files should be provided for color printing? Method One : Draw colored characters on the silkscreen layer of the Gerber and provide reference pictures. For example: Method Two : If you include information about colored silkscreen in the Gerber layer, each individual color must have its own layer. If there is only one layer, we can only print one color. [This method is not recommended] . If you need to print in multiple colors, we recommend using method One and providing us with a reference picture. 4.Please send the images you want to print on the PCB in the following formats: AI, PDF, JPEG, PNG, TIFF, etc., and indicate your desired printing location on the board. 5.If the image contains a QR code, please ensure that the QR code can be accurately scanned and recognized. Note : If you choose UV printing Multi-color, we will use matte UV color printing by default. When designing the colored characters on the bottom layer, be careful not to design the colored characters as mirrored inverses. (The process of color printing is different from that of standard PCB silkscreen printing. When printing colorful characters on the bottom layer, they are printed with the bottom layer of the PCB facing up.) For situations where the entire top or bottom side requires full-color printing, regardless of the solder mask color you choose, we will use a white solder mask on the full-color printed side and then proceed with the color printing. This is for a better printing effect. Please upload the print image, positioning image, and Gerber in one compressed file. By providing a clear positioning image and necessary instructions, you can assist PCBWay in accurately determining and achieving the desired printing position. Matte UV Color Printing vs. Glossy UV Color Printing Matte ink does not increase the overall thickness, and the PCB's appearance looks smooth. Glossy ink increases the overall thickness and may affect the soldering of component pads. The appearance is beautiful but uneven. Features Adopting UV-LED lamp curing, which enables instant drying, can significantly enhances production efficiency. UV printing technology employs UV-curable inks, ensuring firm and clear printing information resistant to fading, thus enhancing product identification and aesthetics. The normal print survives SMT reflow. UV printing technology can present images in various colors and styles, meeting customers' personalized requirements. Professional industrial-grade UV printers support high-precision printing, delivering exquisite results whether on flat panels or rolled materials. Unlike traditional printing methods, UV printing does not produce volatile organic compounds during the production process, ensuring air quality in the production workshop and providing employees with a safer and healthier working environment. FAQ on UV Printing: Can the UV printed surface be cleaned with water? Yes, it can be cleaned with water. Can the UV printed surface be cleaned with alcohol? It is more difficult to clean after being exposed to alcohol and baked (currently, the board undergoes a short baking process after UV printing). However, with increased contact time with alcohol and vigorous scrubbing, it can be removed. This also depends on whether the UV is on the copper surface or the solder mask surface. How hard is the UV printed surface (sensitivity to scratches)? The UV surface is not sensitive to scratches. However, compared to the solder mask, it is less scratch-resistant because UV printing is ink that is sprayed on and is relatively thin. Welcome to give it a try if you're interested! Besides, PCBWay will continue to enhance its manufacturing capabilities to bring more choices and personalized services to customers in the future. If you need to print in multiple colors, we recommend using method One and providing us with a reference picture. 4.Please send the images you want to print on the PCB in the following formats: AI, PDF, JPEG, PNG, TIFF, etc., and indicate your desired printing location on the board. 5.If the image contains a QR code, please ensure that the QR code can be accurately scanned and recognized. Note : If you choose UV printing Multi-color, we will use matte UV color printing by default. When designing the colored characters on the bottom layer, be careful not to design the colored characters as mirrored inverses. (The process of color printing is different from that of standard PCB silkscreen printing. When printing colorful characters on the bottom layer, they are printed with the bottom layer of the PCB facing up.) For situations where the entire top or bottom side requires full-color printing, regardless of the solder mask color you choose, we will use a white solder mask on the full-color printed side and then proceed with the color printing. This is for a better printing effect. Please upload the print image, positioning image, and Gerber in one compressed file. By providing a clear positioning image and necessary instructions, you can assist PCBWay in accurately determining and achieving the desired printing position. Matte UV Color Printing vs. Glossy UV Color Printing Matte ink does not increase the overall thickness, and the PCB's appearance looks smooth. Glossy ink increases the overall thickness and may affect the soldering of component pads. The appearance is beautiful but uneven. Features Adopting UV-LED lamp curing, which enables instant drying, can significantly enhances production efficiency. UV printing technology employs UV-curable inks, ensuring firm and clear printing information resistant to fading, thus enhancing product identification and aesthetics. The normal print survives SMT reflow. UV printing technology can present images in various colors and styles, meeting customers' personalized requirements. Professional industrial-grade UV printers support high-precision printing, delivering exquisite results whether on flat panels or rolled materials. Unlike traditional printing methods, UV printing does not produce volatile organic compounds during the production process, ensuring air quality in the production workshop and providing employees with a safer and healthier working environment. FAQ on UV Printing: Can the UV printed surface be cleaned with water? Yes, it can be cleaned with water. Can the UV printed surface be cleaned with alcohol? It is more difficult to clean after being exposed to alcohol and baked (currently, the board undergoes a short baking process after UV printing). However, with increased contact time with alcohol and vigorous scrubbing, it can be removed. This also depends on whether the UV is on the copper surface or the solder mask surface. How hard is the UV printed surface (sensitivity to scratches)? The UV surface is not sensitive to scratches. However, compared to the solder mask, it is less scratch-resistant because UV printing is ink that is sprayed on and is relatively thin. Welcome to give it a try if you're interested! Verify Now Blog > Ground Stitching Vias in High-Speed PCB Differential Via Design Ground Stitching Vias in High-Speed PCB Differential Via Design by: Mila Aug 25,2026 <dynamic-value> <dynamic-value> Posted in PCB Design & Layout stitching vias differential via design high speed pcb high speed board design In high speed PCB debugging, engineers frequently encounter high-speed link communications failure, severe eye diagram jitter, TDR impedance anomalies near via regions, and EMI radiation exceeding limits by several dBs. After verifying the schematic and trace impedance control, the root cause is often identified: a lack of dedicated stitching vias adjacent to the differential signal vias. 1. Why Return Paths Matter in High Speed Board Design When a signal current flows from the driver to the receiver along a transmission line, an equal and opposite return current travels back through the reference plane. At high frequencies, return current naturally concentrates directly beneath the signal trace to minimize the current loop area. Together, the signal and return currents form a closed loop. A smaller loop area yields lower parasitic inductance, improved signal integrity, and significantly lower EMI radiation. In high speed board design, when a signal transitions between layers or crosses a split plane, maintaining a continuous, minimal return path is essential. (Signal Current + Return Current) 2. How Layer Transitions Disrupt Return Paths When a signal transitions between layers through a via, its reference planes may change, requiring a vertical path for the return current. For instance, if a signal references L2 before a transition and L3 after, the signal current jumps via the signal via. Without stitching vias nearby, no low-impedance vertical bridge exists between L2 and L3. The return current must detour across the reference plane to find a distant ground via, expanding the loop area. This detour leads to three major issues: Higher Parasitic Inductance: Increases loop inductance and degrades high-frequency performance. Impedance Discontinuities: Exacerbates reflections, resulting in ringing and eye diagram degradation. Elevated EMI: Large current loops act as efficient antennas, raising EMI risks. 3. Restoring Return Paths with Stitching Vias Placing stitching vias adjacent to signal vias creates a short, low-impedance vertical path between reference planes. The return current transitions locally through these ground vias rather than taking long detours, maintaining a compact current loop. Ground stitching vias can be through-hole, blind, or buried vias, provided they reliably tie the relevant reference planes together. 4. The Impact of Anti-Pads on Return Current To reduce parasitic capacitance and improve impedance matching, anti-pads are etched into reference planes around signal vias. While anti-pads raise local impedance toward the target (such as 50Ω or 100Ω), excessively large anti-pads remove copper under the via field, forcing the return path outward and increasing loop inductance. Balancing anti-pad sizing with return path continuity is critical in differential via design. 5. Placement Strategies for Stitching Vias Near Anti-Pads Whether addressing plane swaps or anti-pad voids, the objective remains minimizing return path length. Stitching vias should be positioned on the continuous ground copper outside the anti-pad perimeter, rather than inside the void, to ensure immediate vertical coupling for return currents. 6. Key Rules for Differential Via Design in High Speed PCBs Spacing and Pitch: Place stitching vias close to signal vias to maintain path continuity. While a 50-mil pitch serves as a loose rule of thumb for standard rates, ultra-high-speed interfaces (like PCIe 5.0/6.0 or 112G PAM4) demand tighter spacing (often 20–30 mil) validated by SI simulation. Symmetry and Quantity: Place stitching vias symmetrically around differential pairs to mitigate mode conversion ($S_{CD21}$) and absorb common-mode noise. High-speed links may require multiple ground vias forming a via fence around the pair. Layer Connectivity Verification: Confirm that ground vias connect the exact reference layers involved in the transition. Stub Management: Via stubs create parasitic resonance. For high-bandwidth channels, use backdrilling or blind/buried vias to minimize stub lengths. 7.Design Checklist Near-by stitching vias are present at all signal layer transitions. Ground vias correctly bridge the corresponding upper and lower reference planes. Stitching vias are placed symmetrically around differential via pairs. Ground vias sit on solid copper outside the signal via anti-pad voids. Anti-pad dimensions balance via impedance tuning without excessive copper removal. Verify Now Blog > Ground Stitching Vias in High-Speed PCB Differential Via Design Ground Stitching Vias in High-Speed PCB Differential Via Design by: Mila Aug 25,2026 <dynamic-value> <dynamic-value> Posted in PCB Design & Layout stitching vias differential via design high speed pcb high speed board design In high speed PCB debugging, engineers frequently encounter high-speed link communications failure, severe eye diagram jitter, TDR impedance anomalies near via regions, and EMI radiation exceeding limits by several dBs. After verifying the schematic and trace impedance control, the root cause is often identified: a lack of dedicated stitching vias adjacent to the differential signal vias. 1. Why Return Paths Matter in High Speed Board Design When a signal current flows from the driver to the receiver along a transmission line, an equal and opposite return current travels back through the reference plane. At high frequencies, return current naturally concentrates directly beneath the signal trace to minimize the current loop area. Together, the signal and return currents form a closed loop. A smaller loop area yields lower parasitic inductance, improved signal integrity, and significantly lower EMI radiation. In high speed board design, when a signal transitions between layers or crosses a split plane, maintaining a continuous, minimal return path is essential. (Signal Current + Return Current) 2. How Layer Transitions Disrupt Return Paths When a signal transitions between layers through a via, its reference planes may change, requiring a vertical path for the return current. For instance, if a signal references L2 before a transition and L3 after, the signal current jumps via the signal via. Without stitching vias nearby, no low-impedance vertical bridge exists between L2 and L3. The return current must detour across the reference plane to find a distant ground via, expanding the loop area. This detour leads to three major issues: Higher Parasitic Inductance: Increases loop inductance and degrades high-frequency performance. Impedance Discontinuities: Exacerbates reflections, resulting in ringing and eye diagram degradation. Elevated EMI: Large current loops act as efficient antennas, raising EMI risks. 3. Restoring Return Paths with Stitching Vias Placing stitching vias adjacent to signal vias creates a short, low-impedance vertical path between reference planes. The return current transitions locally through these ground vias rather than taking long detours, maintaining a compact current loop. Ground stitching vias can be through-hole, blind, or buried vias, provided they reliably tie the relevant reference planes together. 4. The Impact of Anti-Pads on Return Current To reduce parasitic capacitance and improve impedance matching, anti-pads are etched into reference planes around signal vias. While anti-pads raise local impedance toward the target (such as 50Ω or 100Ω), excessively large anti-pads remove copper under the via field, forcing the return path outward and increasing loop inductance. Balancing anti-pad sizing with return path continuity is critical in differential via design. 5. Placement Strategies for Stitching Vias Near Anti-Pads Whether addressing plane swaps or anti-pad voids, the objective remains minimizing return path length. Stitching vias should be positioned on the continuous ground copper outside the anti-pad perimeter, rather than inside the void, to ensure immediate vertical coupling for return currents. 6. Key Rules for Differential Via Design in High Speed PCBs Spacing and Pitch: Place stitching vias close to signal vias to maintain path continuity. While a 50-mil pitch serves as a loose rule of thumb for standard rates, ultra-high-speed interfaces (like PCIe 5.0/6.0 or 112G PAM4) demand tighter spacing (often 20–30 mil) validated by SI simulation. Symmetry and Quantity: Place stitching vias symmetrically around differential pairs to mitigate mode conversion ($S_{CD21}$) and absorb common-mode noise. High-speed links may require multiple ground vias forming a via fence around the pair. Layer Connectivity Verification: Confirm that ground vias connect the exact reference layers involved in the transition. Stub Management: Via stubs create parasitic resonance. For high-bandwidth channels, use backdrilling or blind/buried vias to minimize stub lengths. 7.Design Checklist Near-by stitching vias are present at all signal layer transitions. Ground vias correctly bridge the corresponding upper and lower reference planes. Stitching vias are placed symmetrically around differential via pairs. Ground vias sit on solid copper outside the signal via anti-pad voids. Anti-pad dimensions balance via impedance tuning without excessive copper removal. Ultra-high-speed differential links are verified via SI simulations for impedance, return path continuity, and mode conversion. Enter the year of your birth and check your Chinese Zodiac. Verify Now Blog > HDI PCB Layout Guide for High Speed Optical Module PCB Design HDI PCB Layout Guide for High Speed Optical Module PCB Design by: Mila Sep 03,2026 <dynamic-value> <dynamic-value> Posted in PCB Design & Layout hdi pcb HDI pcb design optical module pcb high speed pcb layout An optical module PCB is a typical high-frequency, high-density HDI PCB precision board. Its material selection is closely related to transmission rate, link length, loss budget, and device platforms. While 10G and lower modules can use materials like high-Tg FR-4, high-speed modules operating at 25G, 56G, 100G, 400G, and 800G impose stringent requirements on low-loss materials, impedance control, and manufacturing consistency. Below are seven core layout design points and key differences compared to standard PCBs, focusing on high speed pcb layout and practical signal integrity engineering without rigid design fallacies. 1. Substrate Selection and StackUp Design Substrate selection and layer stackup form the foundation for stable high-frequency transmission, directly determining link insertion loss, impedance accuracy, and signal integrity. Multi-Dimensional Rate-Matched Selection: For 25G+ channels, select substrates considering Nyquist frequency, link length, insertion loss budget, dielectric loss, copper foil roughness, and stackup. For long-distance or low-loss channels, choose mid-to-low loss high-speed substrates. Non-critical areas like low-speed control and power can use high-Tg FR-4 to balance performance and cost on an optical module PCB. Adjacent Reference Ground Planes: High-speed differential signal layers should adopt a "signal-reference ground" structure to minimize edge-field coupling. Power layers should pair with adjacent ground layers to optimize PDN impedance via inter-layer capacitance. Pre-Simulation Impedance Modeling: Determine stackup parameters early through SI simulation. The industry standard target is typically 100 ohms differential impedance, with high-performance channels strictly controlling tolerances within +/- 5%. 2. High-Speed Differential TX/RX Signal Integrity High-speed differential signals are the core of data transmission in an optical module PCB. Design should focus on eliminating geometric discontinuities and parasitic interference. Symmetry and Equal Length: Match trace widths, spacing, bends, and via layouts for differential pairs. Advanced HDI pcb design requires controlling intra-pair length skew to prevent differential-to-common mode noise conversion. Trace Geometry Continuity: Use 45-degree angles or smooth arc transitions instead of rigid 90-degree turns. High-frequency reflections stem mostly from vias, pads, stubs, and split reference planes rather than standard trace corners. Minimal Via Structures and Stub Optimization: Minimize layer transitions. For long through-hole structures, apply back-drilling to remove residual stubs, cutting down reflections and resonances. （Backdrill + Via Stub） Unbroken High-Frequency Return Paths: Avoid routing differential traces across ground splits or slot gaps. Provide nearby stitching ground vias whenever signals switch layers. (Differential Pair + Reference Plane + Return Path) Crosstalk Mitigation: Apply the 3W rule during initial layout for proper spacing. For 112G PAM4 ultra-high-speed scenarios, refine trace spacing with 3D EM simulation and add ground via shielding walls where necessary. 3. Optoelectronic Isolation and Sensitive Layout Optical modules combine sensitive analog signals with high-speed digital logic. The analog front-end requires isolation from power and digital noise. Physical Isolation: Separate TOSA/ROSA components and TIA analog circuits from high-speed digital traces and switching power supplies based on form factors (SFP, QSFP, OSFP). Short Analog Traces: Keep weak analog traces from optical devices to TIA and driver ICs as short as possible, avoiding parallel routing alongside high-speed digital lines. Analog Circuit Shielding: Implement localized ground shielding or small metal shields around laser drivers and TIA circuits to isolate high-frequency digital noise. 4. Power Integrity (PI) Optimization Focus on low-impedance return paths, minimal current loops, and sub-region noise reduction. Minimal Loop Decoupling: Configure decoupling networks based on target PDN impedance. Place capacitors close to power pins to minimize parasitic inductance. Solid Ground Plane Priority: Maintain a continuous, low-impedance ground plane across the HDI PCB to provide a solid reference. Apply localized filtering for sensitive analog zones rather than single-point star grounding across the board. Thermal Copper Pour for Power Chips: Place large copper areas with thermal via arrays beneath heat-generating components like laser drivers to disperse heat quickly. 5. Thermal Management in HDI PCB Design Optical module DSPs, optical drivers, and laser diodes generate concentrated heat. High temperatures cause device aging, DK/Df parameter drift, and impedance shifts. Efficient Thermal Paths: Place dense thermal via arrays under high-power devices (DSP, TOSA) to transfer heat from the optical module PCB inner layers to the metal housing. Hot/Cold Component Partitioning: Isolate heat sources from temperature-sensitive optical and clock components to prevent thermal drift and premature aging. Symmetrical Design against Warpage: Balance copper distribution and layer stack-ups across the HDI PCB to manage thermal-mechanical stress during reflow soldering. （Thermal Path IC → Thermal Via → Copper Plane → Housing） 6. EMC and Grounding for High Speed PCB Layout Symmetrical Routing for Common-Mode Noise: Maintain structural symmetry in high-speed differential traces to reduce EMI radiation. Connect the module metal shell to the PCB ground for low-impedance shielding. Interface ESD Protection : Place TVS diodes and common-mode chokes near edge connectors to route ESD currents quickly to chassis ground. Isolate Interference Sources: Keep power inductors and switching regulators away from sensitive RX analog inputs to prevent magnetic coupling. 7. DFM Guidelines for Optical Module PCB Manufacturing Precise HDI pcb design and assembly standards ensure manufacturing yield for dense components. Precision Soldering Design: Use Via-in-Pad or micro-vias for high-density BGAs. For QFN thermal pads, use segmented stencil openings to reduce solder voiding and floating. Optical Alignment Tolerance: Match mechanical outline and mounting hole tolerances precisely with metal housings to avoid optical misalignments. Test Points and Gold Fingers: Keep test points off high-speed trunk lines. Use hard gold plating for edge connector gold fingers to ensure durability across insertion cycles. 8.Optical Module PCB vs Standard PCB Core Differences Enter the year of your birth and check your Chinese Zodiac. Verify Now Blog > High Speed PCB Design Guidelines for Impedance and SI High Speed PCB Design Guidelines for Impedance and SI by: Mila Aug 24,2026 <dynamic-value> <dynamic-value> Posted in PCB Design & Layout pcb design high speed PCB design High-performance board layout is not merely about transmitting signals faster—it is about ensuring they remain stable, continuous, and predictable throughout the entire channel. Verify Now Blog > LDO Output Capacitor Selection: Why Bigger Isn't Always Better in Power Supply Design LDO Output Capacitor Selection: Why Bigger Isn't Always Better in Power Supply Design by: Mila Aug 28,2026 <dynamic-value> <dynamic-value> Posted in PCB Design & Layout power supply design ldo output capacitor output capacitor ldo design ldo layout In power supply design , there is a common engineering misconception regarding the selection of the LDO output capacitor: when faced with issues like high output ripple or poor load transient response, many hardware engineers simply resort to increasing capacitance—upgrading from 10µF to 47µF, then to 220µF, or even paralleling multiple capacitor types at the output. From an energy storage perspective, a larger capacitance supplies more transient charge for the same voltage variation. It seems logical that continually increasing capacitance would indefinitely improve output stability. However, practical engineering often presents a counterintuitive reality. Increasing the capacitance of the LDO output capacitor may not improve stability; instead, it can trigger oscillations, produce periodic voltage fluctuations, or even cause system resets. The root cause is that an LDO is not a simple linear voltage regulator—it is fundamentally a closed-loop control system. The output capacitor does not merely filter noise and store energy; it is an active component of the feedback control loop. Incorrect parameter selection directly compromises overall system stability. 1. Role of the LDO Output Capacitor: Filtering, Energy Storage, and Transient Response A standard LDO design consists of a reference voltage source, an error amplifier, a power pass transistor, a feedback network, and an output capacitor. Its regulation mechanism works as follows: when the output voltage strays from its target, the feedback network detects the error and feeds it into the error amplifier. The amplifier then adjusts the conduction level of the power transistor to tune the output current and bring the voltage back to target. This regulation cycle inherently involves a response time lag. When a step load change occurs—such as a microcontroller switching from sleep mode to full operation, causing the load current to jump from 10mA to 500mA—the LDO cannot instantly adjust its output current due to loop bandwidth limitations. The immediate current deficit is supplied entirely by discharging the LDO output capacitor. Therefore, increasing capacitance theoretically delivers more transient charge and improves transient load response. However, capacitance cannot be increased infinitely because it dictates loop dynamic behavior and directly affects stability margins. （LDO Architecture & Feedback Control Loop. Source: Flywing Tech） 2. How the Output Capacitor Affects LDO Loop Stability In a simplified small-signal model, the output capacitor and the equivalent output load impedance form an output pole, whose frequency is expressed as: f pole = 1 / (2 × π × R OUT × C OUT ) Assuming an output equivalent resistance of 0.1 Ω: a 10µF capacitor creates an output pole at approximately 159 kHz, whereas increasing the capacitor to 100µF shifts the pole down to roughly 15.9 kHz. This calculation illustrates how capacitance influences pole placement; in actual practice, loop poles are also shaped by the pass element, error amplifier, feedback network, and internal compensation circuits. Within any robust power supply design, the output capacitor and its equivalent series resistance (ESR) alter the location of output poles and zeros, dictating crossover frequency and phase margin. As capacitance increases, the output pole moves to lower frequencies, potentially reducing loop crossover frequency or degrading phase margin. Whether this induces oscillation depends on internal compensation, capacitor ESR, load conditions, and phase margin reserves. 3. Requirements Across Different LDO Architectures Because different topologies utilize distinct internal compensation schemes, the requirements for the LDO output capacitor vary significantly across devices. LDOs Requiring ESR Compensation Older architectures rely heavily on the ESR of the output capacitor to introduce a zero into the loop function. This zero cancels phase lag introduced by low-frequency poles, thereby preserving phase margin: fzero = 1 / (2 × π × RESR × COUT) Replacing the output stage with an ultra-low ESR MLCC pushes this ESR zero to much higher frequencies, removing the necessary phase compensation and potentially causing loop instability or severe oscillation. Internally Compensated LDOs Modern LDO design techniques frequently feature internal compensation structures that eliminate strict reliance on ESR, making them fully compatible with low-ESR MLCCs. Nevertheless, capacitance cannot be scaled up without limit. Datasheets still impose recommended maximum capacitance limits because an oversized capacitor shifts loop dynamics, prolongs startup times, and slows fault recovery. 4. Engineering Risks of Over-Sizing Output Capacitors Beyond loop stability issues, an excessively large ldo output capacitor introduces secondary system-level risks. Degraded Startup Characteristics and Overcurrent Triggers During power-up, charging the capacitor requires an inrush current governed by: I inrush = C OUT × (dV OUT / dt) For instance, charging a 470µF capacitor to 3.3V within 10ms demands an average inrush current of roughly 155mA. If this approaches the current limit threshold while simultaneously supplying load current, the LDO may enter current limit mode or fail to start up entirely. Increased Upstream Transient Burden The total charge transferred during startup is defined by: Q = C OUT × V OUT When using soft-start or constant-current limiting mechanisms, a high charge requirement extends startup duration. In systems lacking robust current limiters, large capacitance places severe transient demands on the upstream rail. In an unoptimized power supply design, this inrush can pull down the primary voltage rail and trigger unexpected upstream power-good faults or system resets. 5. Selection Rules for the LDO Output Capacitor Proper component selection requires following datasheet guidelines rather than blindly increasing capacitance values: Recommended Range (Cmin / Cmax): Strictly observe the minimum and maximum recommended values (e.g., 1µF to 10µF) specified in the datasheet to maintain loop stability. ESR Limits: Verify both minimum and maximum ESR constraints, particularly for non-internally compensated regulators. MLCC DC Bias Effects: Multilayer ceramic capacitors experience significant capacitance drops under applied DC operating voltages. Select components based on effective capacitance at the target voltage rather than nominal rating. Temperature and Tolerance Variations: Account for component tolerance over operating temperature extremes to ensure effective capacitance stays within recommended boundaries. Transient Load Demands: If transient load performance is critical, optimize within specified LDO limits. Place local decoupling capacitors close to dynamic loads to handle high-frequency current steps without overloading the LDO feedback loop. Optimized LDO Layout: Trace resistance and parasitic inductance alter output impedance and loop stability. Best practices for ldo layout dictate placing the ldo output capacitor as close as possible to the output and ground pins, minimizing loop area and parasitic effects. Conclusion The core principle for selecting an LDO output capacitor is not "the larger, the better," but rather choosing parameters tailored to operating conditions within specified stability bounds. The output capacitor plays a dual role in energy storage and loop compensation. Blindly increasing capacitance can introduce unexpected loop instability and startup faults. Mastering proper selection alongside a clean LDO layout ensures a reliable, high-performance power supply design. Enter the year of your birth and check your Chinese Zodiac. Select components based on effective capacitance at the target voltage rather than nominal rating. Place local decoupling capacitors close to dynamic loads to handle high-frequency current steps without overloading the LDO feedback loop. Verify Now Blog > PCB Routing Layer Selection for High-Speed Signals: Microstrip vs. Stripline PCB Routing Layer Selection for High-Speed Signals: Microstrip vs. Stripline by: Mila Aug 27,2026 <dynamic-value> <dynamic-value> Posted in PCB Design & Layout pcb design high speed signals high speed signal design high speed signal pcb design high speed design In the hardware layout for high-speed interfaces such as PCIe, DDR5, USB 3.0, and SerDes, selecting the trace layer—specifically choosing between surface microstrip and inner stripline—is a core decision in PCB design, directly impacting signal integrity (SI) and electromagnetic compatibility (EMC). It is important to clarify that interface standards themselves do not explicitly dictate the use of microstrips or striplines. Instead, layer selection relies on a comprehensive balance of total channel performance budgets, stackup structures, manufacturing capabilities, and system-level constraints. There are no universal rules in high speed signal design. 1. Structure and Electrical Characteristics of Microstrip and Stripline Stripline (Inner Layer Routing) A stripline places the signal trace between two complete reference planes, confining the electric field within the internal substrate between these planes. Its inherent characteristics include: Crosstalk and Shielding: In a homogeneous medium, symmetric striplines offer a natural advantage in suppressing Far-End Crosstalk (FEXT). Under ideal structural conditions, the field symmetry significantly reduces FEXT. Outer electromagnetic radiation is generally lower, and susceptibility to external electromagnetic fields is reduced. In real-world engineering, factors like dielectric asymmetry, localized dielectric constant fluctuations from fiber weave, adjacent layer coupling, trace bends, and via structures break this ideal symmetrical environment, meaning FEXT cannot be completely eliminated. Transmission Uniformity: Because the electric field is largely contained inside the PCB dielectric, the propagation environment is relatively uniform. It is generally less susceptible to local dielectric constant variations compared to surface microstrips, though fiber-weave effects still exist. Propagation Velocity: The electric field is mainly confined to the dielectric region between the upper and lower reference planes. The effective dielectric constant is closer to that of the raw substrate material. Consequently, signal propagation velocity is relatively lower, resulting in higher propagation delay. Microstrip (Outer Layer Routing) A microstrip trace sits on the outer layer, with dielectric substrate on one side and air on the other. The electric field is split between the substrate and the air. Its inherent characteristics include: Crosstalk and Radiation: Compared to ideal symmetric striplines, microstrips usually exhibit more noticeable FEXT coupling. However, microstrips do not automatically imply poor EMI performance. The root factors driving radiation levels are current loop area, return path continuity, signal edge rates, and structural discontinuities—not simply being on the surface layer. With continuous return paths and proper layout, radiation from short surface differential traces can be kept well within compliance limits. Propagation Velocity: Because part of the electric field travels through air, the effective dielectric constant is lower than the substrate material itself. This results in faster signal propagation and lower propagation delay. 2. Engineering Trade-offs Between Microstrip and Stripline From a pure electromagnetic perspective, symmetric striplines offer superior transmission and shielding. However, in real-world implementations, inner-layer routing requires via transitions. The vertical transition penalty often offsets the theoretical advantages of striplines. Choosing between them is fundamentally a trade-off between better field confinement and simpler pin escape with fewer vertical transitions in high speed signal PCB design. Performance and Cost Impacts of Via Vertical Transitions Component pins are typically located on the surface. Routing a high speed signal to an inner stripline layer requires via transitions. The vertical interconnect—comprising the via, stub, pads, and anti-pads—can introduce impedance discontinuities that degrade channel performance. Via Stub Effects: For high-speed interfaces like PCIe Gen4 and DDR5, long via stubs cause significant impedance discontinuities and resonances. Under proper stackups, methods like backdrilling or blind/buried vias are used to control stub length. Deciding whether to backdrill requires evaluating PCB thickness, via types, stub length, signal spectrum, Nyquist frequency, and impedance targets through simulation. Return Path Continuity: When changing layers alters the reference plane, the return path must be planned synchronously. Placing ground vias near signal transitions provides a low-impedance path for high-frequency return currents. If reference properties are consistent across layers, return path impacts are minimized. Design Complexity: Well-optimized via transitions achieve smooth impedance continuity, whereas unoptimized vias introduce reflection and insertion loss. Every extra layer change adds a vertical node needing refined layout and simulation work. In short-distance chip-to-chip routing, surface traces allow direct pin escape without vias, maintaining continuous impedance without stub risks. In such cases, a via-free microstrip often outperforms an inner stripline with unoptimized via transitions. Propagation Delay and Timing Matching Due to velocity differences between microstrips and striplines, mixed-layer routing cannot rely solely on physical length matching. Delay compensation based on actual stackup parameters is essential for effective high speed design. Striplines have higher effective dielectric constants, leading to higher unit-length propagation delay than microstrips. Actual delay should be calculated using dielectric properties and trace geometry rather than fixed rule-of-thumb numbers. Routing critical signals within the same layer structure minimizes propagation delay variances, making length matching far more straightforward. Testability and Debugging Convenience During early development phases where critical nodes require probing, surface traces allow easier access for test points and probe pads. Oscilloscope and high-speed probes can directly sample signal waveforms. Striplines are shielded by reference copper layers, preventing direct probing on the trace. Testing requires pre-designed test vias or connector interfaces. Therefore, surface microstrips offer a clear advantage for rapid iteration and debug cycles. Overall Stackup Resource Allocation Inner routing resources must be balanced across high-speed signals, power planes, and solid reference planes. For modern multilayer boards, inner striplines are vital routing areas for high speed signals rather than simple low-speed layers. When component placement, return paths, and EMI requirements permit, placing some differential pairs on outer layers frees up inner resources for power planes and critical inner-layer routing. Target Impedance Process Windows In common stackup configurations, striplines are constrained by dual reference planes, requiring narrower trace widths to achieve target differential impedance. Microstrips offer wider geometry windows, meaning wider trace widths and more forgiving fabrication tolerances for the same target impedance. This is not absolute; impedance feasibility depends on stackup parameters, dielectric constants, copper weight, and PCB vendor capabilities. Some stackup designs easily accommodate target impedances on striplines as well. 3. Typical Application Scenarios There is no mandatory scenario requiring one exact structure. Through proper shielding, via optimization, and reference plane design, both structures can meet system goals. However, each structure excels in specific contexts. Scenarios Preferring Surface Microstrip Short chip-to-chip direct links with both devices on the surface layer. Projects aiming to minimize vertical transitions and reduce via simulation workload. Prototype development requiring frequent physical signal probing. Designs with moderate EMI/EMC constraints where proper return path layout keeps radiation controlled. Layouts with sufficient outer layer space and low crosstalk risk. Scenarios Preferring Inner Stripline Long-distance on-board traces with extended parallel coupling lengths. High-density, multi-bus routing with high crosstalk exposure. Products with strict EMI/EMC compliance requirements demanding low radiation. Environments with severe external electromagnetic interference needing strong shielding. Backplane interconnects and high-density SerDes channels requiring strict crosstalk control. 4. Selection Guidelines for Microstrip and Stripline Rather than deciding purely on single factors like "high-speed" or "long-distance," evaluate the complete channel when executing high speed signal design: Signal Rate and Distance Evaluate rise/fall times, data rates, and physical length. Short links benefit from microstrip routing to avoid vias; long links require striplines for loss and crosstalk control. Vias and Vertical Transitions When changing layers, analyze via count, stub lengths, pad/anti-pad dimensions, and reference continuity. Optimize transitions via simulation and use backdrilling or blind/buried vias where necessary. Reference Planes and Return Paths Ensure continuous, low-impedance reference paths. Use ground return vias when switching layers across different reference planes. Crosstalk and EMI Requirements Evaluate NEXT and FEXT for long parallel runs. Use stripline for strict EMC targets. If using microstrip, increase spacing and shorten parallel runs. PCB Stackup and Fabrication Capability Match layer choice with stackup thickness, dielectric constants, and trace width limits. Verify that target impedance falls within vendor manufacturing windows. Debugging Needs Consider hardware testing requirements early. Microstrip routes accommodate direct probing, whereas striplines require explicit test structures. Final Selection Summary Prioritize Microstrip: Short distances, surface chip-to-chip links, minimal via requirements, high debug needs, and manageable EMI/crosstalk risks. Prioritize Stripline: Long distances, dense parallel traces, crosstalk sensitivity, strict EMC requirements, or harsh EMI environments. Both Are Viable: For standard links, both structures work well provided stackup, impedance, return paths, and via transitions are correctly designed. 5. Common Misconceptions Misconception: Stripline signal integrity is always superior to microstrip. Clarification: Overall performance depends on the entire channel. A stripline with unoptimized via transitions may perform worse than a surface microstrip due to added impedance discontinuities and stub losses. Misconception: Surface high-speed traces inevitably cause EMI compliance failures. Clarification: Radiation depends primarily on current loop area, return path continuity, and edge rates. Short differential microstrips with solid reference planes easily pass EMC standards. Conclusion Selecting between surface microstrip and inner stripline in PCB design involves no absolute optimal choice or rigid rules. The objective is not choosing a "theoretically perfect" structure, but selecting the scheme that optimizes full channel performance under system-level constraints. Stripline offers superior shielding and crosstalk suppression at the cost of via complexity; microstrip offers simple escape, continuous impedance, easy debugging, and wider manufacturing windows. Final layer selection should always be verified by full-channel simulation and manufacturing capabilities. Enter the year of your birth and check your Chinese Zodiac. Verify Now Blog > Power Supply Capacitor Layout: Placement Rules for Bulk and Small Capacitors Power Supply Capacitor Layout: Placement Rules for Bulk and Small Capacitors by: Mila Aug 25,2026 <dynamic-value> <dynamic-value> Posted in PCB Design & Layout power supply design power supply capacitor capacitor placement capacitor layout decoupling capacitor placement Engineers often encounter hard-to-spot issues when debugging switch-mode power supplies, DC-DC converters, and LDO circuits. These issues typically stem from placing electrolytic or tantalum bulk capacitors alongside 0402 or 0603 small ceramic capacitors arbitrarily. Symptoms include high power supply ripple, significant voltage sags during load transients, timing anomalies in high-speed ICs, and ADC sampling noise drift. Incorrect placement degrades power performance and expands high-frequency current loop areas, elevating EMC risks. While parallel configurations of bulk and ceramic capacitors are common knowledge, their spatial placement rules are frequently misunderstood. Below is a breakdown of layout principles based on capacitor impedance characteristics and Power Distribution Network (PDN) design. 1.Power Ssupply Capacitor Differences: Bulk vs. Ceramic Capacitors A capacitor’s behavior in a power network depends not only on capacitance, but also on Equivalent Series Resistance (ESR), Equivalent Series Inductance (ESL), Self-Resonating Frequency (SRF), and PCB parasitics. Bulk Capacitors (Electrolytic / Tantalum, μF to mF ange) Store large amounts of charge to handle low-frequency load current changes and suppress low-frequency voltage fluctuations. Larger packages introduce higher lead ESL. Above their SRF, they exhibit inductive properties and lose low impedance at high frequencies. Small Ceramic Capacitors (nF to μF range) Low ESL MLCCs maintain low impedance at higher frequencies, making them ideal for suppressing MHz switch noise and high-frequency transient interference. High-frequency performance is sensitive to trace parasitics; excessively long traces negate their low ESL advantage. Note: Operating bands cannot be defined solely by capacitance. A 10 μF MLCC may outperform a 100 μF electrolytic capacitor at high frequencies due to lower ESL. Effective capacitance in MLCCs is also reduced by DC bias, operating temperature, and voltage. 2.Core Capacitor Layout Principles: Lowering PDN Impedance and Parasitics Connecting capacitors in parallel does not mean current flows through one before reaching the other. The goal of a Power Distribution Network is to keep PDN impedance (Z PDN ) below a target threshold: Z PDN = V noise / I transient Lower PDN impedance reduces voltage noise (Vnoise) during transient current spikes (Itransient). At lower frequencies, trace inductive reactance (X L = 2π f L) remains minimal, allowing bulk capacitors to supply charge even when placed further away. As frequency rises, parasitic inductance grows rapidly. Proper decoupling capacitor placement demands placing low-ESL ceramic components as close to the IC power pins as possible to minimize loop area and lower high-frequency impedance. Key High-Frequency Loops: IC Decoupling Loop: IC Power Pin → MLCC → GND → IC GND Pin. DC-DC Power Loop: High d i /d t loops formed by switching elements, input bypass capacitors, power inductors, and return paths. Optimizing capacitor layout requires prioritizing high d i /d t loops in DC-DC converters, while IC decoupling requires shortening the supply and return paths between the load and the MLCC. Placement Rule: Position low-ESL ceramic capacitors closest to IC power pins. Place bulk energy storage capacitors near power inlets or DC-DC / LDO output pins. Converter Exceptions: DC-DC output capacitors are part of the control loop and power filter. They must strictly follow datasheet requirements and sit near converter pins. LDO capacitors must also strictly align with datasheet ESR and placement specifications. Routing: Avoid routing traces serially from bulk to small capacitors and then to the IC pin, as this lengthens the high-frequency loop. Connect both capacitors directly to the power plane with short traces. 3.Practical Capacitor Placement Guidelines DC-DC and LDO Input Placement: Place bulk capacitors at the input for local energy storage and low-frequency ripple suppression based on datasheet recommendations. Position low-ESL ceramic capacitors directly adjacent to the VIN pin. DC-DC and LDO Output Placement: Prioritize datasheet guidelines for output power supply capacitor selection. Place small ceramic capacitors close to converter VOUT pins or load IC pins to suppress switching noise. Minimize Buck converter power loop areas. Proximity Rule for Small Ceramic Capacitors: Shorten both power and GND current paths. A short power trace paired with a long return path degrades high-frequency decoupling. Low-Impedance Grounding: Connect capacitor GND terminals to a continuous reference plane using short, low-inductance paths. Place GND vias directly adjacent to component pads. Multi-Stage Filtering: Avoid mechanically sorting capacitors strictly by size and distance. Place bulk capacitors near power inputs and low-ESL MLCCs near sensitive loads. When adding ferrite beads for multi-stage filtering on sensitive rails (e.g., ADC or RF), evaluate potential impedance resonances between the bead and adjacent capacitors. 4.Power Supply Capacitor Layout Checklist Place low-ESL ceramic decoupling capacitors closest to IC power pins. Follow datasheet specifications for DC-DC and LDO input/output capacitor parameters and layout. Avoid serial routing that forces current sequentially through capacitors. Keep power and ground traces as short as possible to minimize high-frequency loop areas. Connect capacitor ground terminals with short paths and vias adjacent to pads. Minimize high d i /d t power loop areas in DC-DC converters. Ensure LDO output capacitor ESR falls within the specified stability range. Validate multi-stage filter layouts against PDN impedance targets rather than relying on basic capacity-to-distance rules. Enter the year of your birth and check your Chinese Zodiac. These issues typically stem from insufficient material support in the bend zone, cutouts positioned too close to the bend line, and stress concentration at corners. By optimizing flange length, cutout positioning, and bend relief structures during the design stage, you can eliminate the risk of bending deformation at the source and achieve consistent precision and structural integrity. 1. Ensure Adequate Support Length for Flanges Sheet metal bending relies on upper and lower tooling to apply forming forces, which requires flanges on both sides of the bend line to have sufficient length to form a continuous, stable load-bearing surface. Insufficient flange length prevents the sheet metal from receiving adequate die support, leading to material slipping, stretching, or localized collapse during bending. Different material thicknesses impose distinct requirements on minimum flange length and support coverage across the total bend length: Sheet metal ≤ 0.135 in (3.43 mm): At least 50% of the total bend length must meet the minimum flange length requirement on both sides of the bend line. Medium-thick plate at 0.187 in (4.75 mm) and 0.250 in (6.35 mm): Both flanges must meet the minimum flange length requirement across 100% of the total bend length. Thicker materials require higher forming forces, making continuous flange support even more critical. If support length is insufficient, thick plates are prone to material shift, over-stretching, and out-of-tolerance bend angles. 2. Control Cutout Placement and Coverage Ratio in Bend Zones Placing holes, notches, edge cutouts, or other feature cuts too close to the bend line causes severe feature distortion due to plastic material flow during sheet metal bending. This also weakens structural strength within the bend zone, further magnifying bending deformation risks. For standard air bending processes, cutouts should generally maintain a safety distance of at least 1/2 of the lower V-die opening width from the bend line to keep features outside the primary tooling engagement zone. Specific clearance requirements should be verified based on material type, sheet thickness, and actual tooling parameters. Designers can use manufacturing simulation software to flag high-risk deformation zones and validate feature placement. In addition to safety distance, you must limit the total percentage of cutouts within the bend warning zone to maintain adequate material support: Materials ≤ 0.135 in (3.43 mm): Cutout coverage within the bend zone should not exceed 50%. Materials ≥ 0.187 in (4.75 mm): A minimum of 85% solid, unbroken material must be retained across the bend length. 3. Implement Proper Bend Relief and Clearance Features When a bend meets a part corner or when adjacent bends are spaced too closely, the material at the corner experiences multi-axial stress concentration. This frequently results in severe wrinkling, material bulging, or corner tearing. Standard DFM for sheet metal provides two effective solutions for these scenarios: Relocate the bend line: Move the bend line away from nearby cutouts or adjacent bends whenever structural constraints allow. This expands the solid material area within the forming zone and redistributes forming stresses. Add dedicated bend relief features: Incorporate relief cuts or corner reliefs at bend ends and intersecting corners. This relieves stress concentration, provides necessary clearance for material flow, prevents corner bulging and adjacent flange interference, and minimizes tearing risks. 4. Adapt Design Guidelines to Material Characteristics Formability varies significantly across material grades; standard design parameters cannot be universally applied without adjustments. Non-metallic sheets (e.g., PMMA): Follow specialized rules for bend radii, flange lengths, and relief structures. Polycarbonate is particularly prone to cracking along bend lines and must not be designed using standard metallic DFM for sheet metal rules. Heavy-gauge metal plates: Higher tonnage requirements demand stricter flange support. Avoid placing large, asymmetrical, or square cutouts within the active tooling engagement area to mitigate risks of stretching, tearing, and warping. 5. Sheet Metal Bending DFM Checklist Review these essential checklist items prior to submitting your design for manufacturing: Does the flange length meet the minimum requirement for the specified material and thickness? Are holes, slots, notches, and cutouts kept at a safe clearance distance from the bend line? Is the cutout coverage ratio within the bend warning zone compliant with thickness limits? Are proper bend relief cuts provided at bend terminations and corner intersections? Are large, square, or asymmetrical cutouts avoided within the tooling zone on thick plates? Are adjacent bends evaluated for structural interference and stress accumulation risks? Do non-metallic parts (such as polycarbonate) follow material-specific bending guidelines? Have you verified your model against the manufacturing platform's automated DFM and design rules? Conclusion Preventing bending deformation fundamentally relies on matching part design to the physical forces of the sheet metal bending process. Following robust DFM for sheet metal principles guarantees continuous material support and structural strength throughout the forming zone. Compliant designs prevent cosmetic and structural defects, improve dimensional consistency, and significantly cut prototyping rework costs. Enter the year of your birth and check your Chinese Zodiac.
